correctness.rationale: An induced horizontal edge consumes one row and two columns, and a vertical edge consumes two rows and one column; distinct edges cannot reuse any consumed coordinate because an endpoint would be adjacent to an endpoint of another edge. Conversely disjoint coordinate packets yield induced matchings. Choosing ordered row/column coordinates and pairing gives exactly m!n!/[2^(h+v)h!v!(m-h-2v)!(n-2h-v)!], with h+2v<=m and 2h+v<=n. Existence of h,v for t=h+v reduces to max(0,2t-n)<=v<=min(t,m-t), giving t<=min(m,n,floor((m+n)/3)). In a strong total cover selecting vertex set X, unselected U, required internal edges and one crossing edge for each isolated U vertex force cost>=|V|-|U|+|E(G[U])|+isolates(U). Each nontrivial component contributes <=1 to |U|-edges-isolates; one edge per component is an induced matching. Equality yields the known general minimum |V|-alpha_ind. For the two-row family n>=4, equality forces two disjoint induced K2 components in different rows with four distinct columns and no U isolates; choosing two disjoint column pairs gives binomial product. For width 2 and 3, enumerate U induced path and isolates, obtaining 8 and 45. Independent raw-graph enumeration confirms six polynomial instances plus two-row n2..7 cover counts, but infinite proof is combinatorial.
residual_risks: Strong total cover definition must include a selected edge covering itself and both endpoints; different edge-cover conventions invalidate the formula.
The exact n=3 count includes crossing-edge multiplicity three for each extra isolated vertex, not just the six U subsets.
